name: Backend & Databases
blurb: Postgres schema and query tuning, API design, auth, and the Supabase, Neon, Prisma, Stripe, Firebase and NoSQL details that bite.

tests.prompt: Design tables for a multi-tenant invoicing app on Supabase.
tests.good: bigint identity PKs plus UUID public ids, tenant_id with composite indexes, FKs indexed, numeric or cents for money, timestamptz, RLS on every table with (select auth.uid()) and WITH CHECK on updates.

tests.prompt: Our orders list endpoint got slow at page 500.
tests.good: Asks for explain (analyze, buffers), replaces OFFSET with cursor pagination on (created_at, id), adds a matching composite index, caps limit at 100.

tests.prompt: Add Stripe subscriptions to our Next.js app.
tests.good: Uses Checkout Sessions with dynamic payment methods, verifies webhook signatures on the raw body, grants access from subscription and invoice events idempotently, pins the API version, keeps secret keys server-side.

tests.prompt: Build the API and Postgres schema for a booking app for dog groomers: salons, groomers, appointments and card deposits through Stripe. Neon for the database, Fastify for the API, deployed to Cloud Run. Give me a threat model before launch.
tests.good: States a short plan first: schema, API and payments here (postgres-schema.md, neon.md, api-design.md, stripe.md), the container and deploy through cloud-devops (docker.md and gcp.md: non-root image on 0.0.0.0:$PORT, secrets from Secret Manager, a dedicated service account), the threat model through security (threat-modeling.md: data-flow diagram and STRIDE over the booking and payment flows). Pooled Neon URL for the app, direct URL for migrations; a database constraint against double booking; deposits granted from verified webhooks, idempotent by event id; checks the Done means of all three crafts.
